title: Acts Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Acts 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Prayer and ministry of the word
questions.explanation: The murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews is mentioned first in Acts 6:1.

questions.question: What was the reason for the murmuring of the Grecians?
questions.explanation: The verse states that the Grecians murmured because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration (Acts 6:1).

questions.question: Who called the multitude of the disciples together?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:2 indicates that the twelve called the multitude of the disciples unto them.

questions.question: What did the twelve apostles express was not reasonable for them to do?
questions.explanation: The apostles said it was not reasonable for them to leave the word of God (Acts 6:2).

questions.question: What did the apostles ask the brethren to look for?
questions.explanation: In Acts 6:3, the apostles instructed the brethren to look out among them seven men of honest report.

questions.question: What qualities were the seven men supposed to have?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 specifies that the seven men were to be of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom.

questions.question: What will the apostles give themselves continually to?
options: Prayer and ministry of the word
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and ministry of the word
questions.explanation: Acts 6:4 states that the apostles will give themselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the multitude to the apostles' saying?
questions.explanation: According to Acts 6:5, the saying pleased the whole multitude.

questions.question: Who was chosen as one of the seven men?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 mentions that they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the chosen seven men?
questions.explanation: Matthew is not mentioned as one of the chosen men in Acts 6:5; the chosen ones include Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas.

questions.question: What was Nicolas's background?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 identifies Nicolas as a proselyte of Antioch.

questions.question: True or False: The Grecians were complaining about the neglect of their widows.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1 states that there arose a murmuring of the Grecians because their widows were neglected.

questions.question: True or False: The twelve apostles decided to serve tables.
questions.explanation: The apostles stated in Acts 6:2 that it was not reasonable for them to leave the word of God and serve tables.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles chose twelve men to handle the daily ministration.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 indicates they appointed seven men, not twelve, over this business.

questions.question: True or False: All the chosen men were from Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 mentions Nicolas as a proselyte of Antioch, indicating not all were from Jerusalem.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the apostles do after setting forth the seven men before them?
options: They prayed and laid their hands on them
They sent them to preach to the Gentiles
They instructed them to serve tables only
They asked them to fast for three days
questions.correctAnswer: They prayed and laid their hands on them
questions.explanation: Acts 6:6 says they prayed and laid their hands on them after setting them before the apostles.

questions.question: What does Acts 6:7 promise will happen if someone prays and lays hands on chosen men as in Acts 6:6?
options: The word of God will increase and disciples multiply
The widows will be served immediately
questions.correctAnswer: The word of God will increase and disciples multiply
questions.explanation: Acts 6:7 states that after the laying on of hands and prayer, the word of God increased and the number of disciples multiplied.

questions.question: What was Stephen full of, which enabled him to do wonders and miracles?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:8 describes Stephen as being full of faith and power, which enabled his miracles.

questions.question: How did Stephen respond when certain synagogue members disputed with him?
options: He spoke with wisdom and the Spirit
He asked the apostles to intervene
questions.correctAnswer: He spoke with wisdom and the Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 6:10 says they were unable to resist the wisdom and the Spirit by which Stephen spoke.

questions.question: What practical lesson can we learn from the apostles choosing men 'full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom' to serve tables?
options: Spiritual leadership requires both character and wisdom
Only apostles can serve the church
Physical service is less important than preaching
Ministry roles should be assigned randomly
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual leadership requires both character and wisdom
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 emphasizes choosing men full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, highlighting needed qualities for service.

questions.question: What was the cause of murmuring among the disciples according to Acts 6:1?
options: Widows of the Grecians were neglected
The apostles were not preaching enough
questions.correctAnswer: Widows of the Grecians were neglected
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1 explains the murmuring arose because the Grecian widows were neglected.

questions.question: What attitude did the whole multitude have toward the choice of Stephen and the other seven men?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 states that the saying pleased the whole multitude.

questions.question: Which groups opposed Stephen's message according to Acts 6:9?
options: Libertines, Cyrenians, Alexandrians, Cilicians, and Asians
questions.correctAnswer: Libertines, Cyrenians, Alexandrians, Cilicians, and Asians
questions.explanation: Acts 6:9 lists these groups as disputing with Stephen.

questions.question: What does the inability of Stephen's opponents to resist his wisdom and Spirit imply for Christian conduct today?
options: Spiritual wisdom and reliance on the Spirit are powerful defenses
Arguments should be avoided at all costs
Physical strength is more important than wisdom
Disputes prove a lack of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual wisdom and reliance on the Spirit are powerful defenses
questions.explanation: Acts 6:10 shows that wisdom and the Spirit make one’s defense unassailable.

questions.question: How did the apostles prioritize their responsibilities according to Acts 6:2-4?
options: Prayer and ministry of the word over serving tables
Ignoring prayer to manage daily needs
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and ministry of the word over serving tables
questions.explanation: Acts 6:2-4 shows apostles wanted to focus on prayer and ministry of the word rather than serving tables.

questions.question: What quality made Stephen suitable for his role, as reflected in both Acts 6:5 and Acts 6:8?
options: Full of faith and the Holy Ghost
questions.correctAnswer: Full of faith and the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 and 6:8 describe Stephen as full of faith and the Holy Ghost.

questions.question: What is the practical result of the apostles’ decision to appoint men to serve tables, according to Acts 6:7?
options: The word of God increased and disciples multiplied
questions.correctAnswer: The word of God increased and disciples multiplied
questions.explanation: Acts 6:7 connects appointing men for service with growth in the word and disciples.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 6:7, a great company of priests became obedient to the faith as a result of the ministry.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:7 states that a great company of the priests were obedient to the faith.

questions.question: True or False: According to Acts 6:1, the apostles ignored the murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews because they prioritized preaching only.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1 shows the murmuring existed, and Acts 6:2-4 shows apostles addressed it by appointing men to serve.

questions.question: True or False: Stephen's opponents were able to successfully refute his arguments because they had equal wisdom and spirit according to Acts 6:10.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:10 states they were not able to resist the wisdom and spirit by which Stephen spoke.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 6.

questions.question: What accusation was made against Stephen by the false witnesses?
options: He spoke blasphemous words against Moses and God
He denied the resurrection of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: He spoke blasphemous words against Moses and God
questions.explanation: Acts 6:11 states that they suborned men to say they heard Stephen speak blasphemous words against Moses and God.

questions.question: Who stirred up the people against Stephen?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:12 mentions that the elders and scribes came upon Stephen and caught him, stirring up the people.

questions.question: What did the false witnesses claim Stephen said about Jesus of Nazareth?
options: He is the Son of God
He will return to judge the world
questions.explanation: Acts 6:14 records that the false witnesses claimed Stephen said Jesus of Nazareth shall destroy this place.

questions.question: How did the council perceive Stephen during his trial?
options: He had the face of an angel
questions.correctAnswer: He had the face of an angel
questions.explanation: Acts 6:15 describes how all that sat in the council saw Stephen's face as it had been the face of an angel.

questions.question: What was Stephen full of, according to Acts 6:8?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:8 states that Stephen was full of faith and power, doing great wonders and miracles among the people.

questions.question: What did the apostles prioritize over serving tables?
options: Prayer and ministry of the word
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and ministry of the word
questions.explanation: Acts 6:4 indicates that the apostles prioritized giving themselves continually to prayer and the ministry of the word.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'blasphemous' in Acts 6:11 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'blasphemous' (blasphemous) means to speak evil or slander, which is relevant to the accusations against Stephen.

questions.question: Which literary device is exhibited when the council sees Stephen's face as that of an angel?
questions.explanation: The description of Stephen's face as that of an angel employs vivid imagery to convey his divine favor and calmness amidst accusations.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of false testimony against a righteous person?
questions.explanation: Matthew 26:60-61 describes false witnesses being sought against Jesus, echoing the false accusations made against Stephen.

questions.question: Which other passage speaks of the wisdom of Stephen that could not be resisted?
questions.explanation: Acts 7:10 mentions how God gave Stephen wisdom that his adversaries could not withstand, reflecting the theme found in Acts 6:10.

questions.question: What comes before the accusation against Stephen in Acts 6:11?
options: The selection of the seven men
questions.explanation: Acts 6:10 precedes the accusation in verse 11, stating that Stephen performed great wonders and miracles, which led to the opposition.

questions.question: What is the significance of the number seven in the selection of deacons?
questions.explanation: The number seven often symbolizes perfection or completion in biblical literature, suggesting a sense of divine order in appointing the deacons.

questions.question: Stephen's name means what in Hebrew?
questions.explanation: The name Stephen comes from the Greek 'Stephanos', meaning 'crown', which is significant given his later martyrdom.

questions.question: True or False: The apostles decided they should serve tables instead of preaching.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:2 indicates that the apostles believed it was not reasonable for them to leave the word of God to serve tables, thereby affirming their commitment to preaching.

questions.question: True or False: Stephen was accused of speaking against the law.
questions.explanation: Acts 6:13 states that false witnesses claimed Stephen spoke against the law, confirming the truth of the accusation.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 6:4 teach about the apostles' understanding of sanctification and ministry?
options: The apostles prioritized prayer and the ministry of the word over administrative tasks
The apostles believed serving tables was the highest form of sanctification
Sanctification was only about external ritual observance
The apostles rejected prayer as unnecessary for ministry
questions.correctAnswer: The apostles prioritized prayer and the ministry of the word over administrative tasks
questions.explanation: Acts 6:4 shows the apostles committing themselves continually to prayer and the ministry of the word, indicating sanctification involves spiritual devotion and proclamation rather than mere service tasks.

questions.question: What doctrine about the guidance of the Holy Spirit in church leadership is taught in Acts 6:3?
options: Church leaders should be full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom
Leaders are chosen based on wealth and social status
Human wisdom alone suffices for church leadership
Spiritual gifts are irrelevant for leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Church leaders should be full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 instructs selecting seven men full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, indicating that divine empowerment and discernment are essential for church leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning human sin and opposition to the gospel is seen in Acts 6:9–10?
options: Unbelief manifests as opposition even from diverse cultural groups
Sinful opposition is always overcome by human wisdom alone
Only physical enemies oppose the gospel, not synagogue members
Opposition to the gospel proves the truth of the message
questions.correctAnswer: Unbelief manifests as opposition even from diverse cultural groups
questions.explanation: Acts 6:9–10 describes how members from various synagogues opposed Stephen, showing that human sin causes rejection of the gospel despite its divine wisdom and Spirit.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 6:8 specifically demonstrate in the ministry of Stephen?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:8 states Stephen was full of faith and power, doing great wonders and miracles, demonstrating God's attribute of power manifested through His servant.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by the apostles' prayer before appointing the seven men in Acts 6:6?
questions.explanation: In Acts 6:6, the apostles prayed before laying hands on the seven men, showing God's sovereign appointment and blessing over church leaders.

questions.question: How does the appointment of the seven in Acts 6 prepare for the broader New Testament theme of the priesthood of all believers?
options: It decentralizes ministry functions beyond the apostles, anticipating shared priestly duties
It establishes a rigid hierarchy where only apostles minister
It limits ministry to Jewish believers only
It excludes the Holy Spirit from church governance
questions.correctAnswer: It decentralizes ministry functions beyond the apostles, anticipating shared priestly duties
questions.explanation: Acts 6 shows the apostles delegating responsibilities to appointed men, reflecting the New Testament doctrine that all believers share in priestly ministry (cf. 1 Peter 2:9).

questions.question: In what way does the opposition to Stephen in Acts 6:11-14 fulfill Old Testament patterns of prophetic rejection?
options: False witnesses accuse him of blasphemy, similar to prophets like Jeremiah
Stephen is accepted without dispute as all prophets were
The people immediately repent and honor Stephen
Stephen’s opponents affirm his teachings publicly
questions.correctAnswer: False witnesses accuse him of blasphemy, similar to prophets like Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Acts 6:11-14 shows Stephen being falsely accused, paralleling the rejection and false accusations faced by OT prophets such as Jeremiah (Jeremiah 20:1-2).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 6:1 and 6:3 teach about the nature of church order and communal responsibility?
options: The church must organize practical care to maintain unity and focus on spiritual ministry
Church order is irrelevant and spontaneous
Only apostles bear responsibility for all church tasks
Neglect of widows is acceptable if the word is preached
questions.correctAnswer: The church must organize practical care to maintain unity and focus on spiritual ministry
questions.explanation: Acts 6:1 describes a dispute over neglected widows; Acts 6:3 shows appointing men to oversee this, reflecting doctrine that practical care supports spiritual unity and mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the Spirit and wisdom is taught by Acts 6:3 and Acts 6:10?
options: Effective ministry requires being full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom which cannot be resisted
Wisdom is unnecessary if one has the Spirit
Human wisdom alone is sufficient to refute opposition
The Spirit is unrelated to wisdom in ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Effective ministry requires being full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom which cannot be resisted
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 prescribes men full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, and Acts 6:10 shows opponents unable to resist Stephen's Spirit-filled wisdom, teaching their inseparability in ministry.

questions.question: What does the combination of Acts 6:5 and Acts 6:7 teach about the relationship between visible spiritual leadership and church growth?
options: Spirit-empowered leaders contribute to the increase of disciples and obedience
Church growth is independent of leadership qualities
Growth depends only on external cultural factors
questions.correctAnswer: Spirit-empowered leaders contribute to the increase of disciples and obedience
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 shows choosing men full of faith and the Holy Ghost; Acts 6:7 reports growth in disciples and obedience, indicating Spirit-filled leadership fosters church expansion.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Acts 6:11-14 shows the early church using false accusations to silence opposition. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Opponents suborned false witnesses against Stephen, indicating human opposition to the gospel often resorts to lies
The church sanctioned false accusations as a method of control
False accusations were divinely inspired to test faith
questions.correctAnswer: Opponents suborned false witnesses against Stephen, indicating human opposition to the gospel often resorts to lies
questions.explanation: Acts 6:11-14 narrates how opponents maliciously arranged false witnesses, demonstrating sinful hostility toward the gospel rather than church-sanctioned deception.

questions.question: What doctrine about the inclusivity of the gospel is implied by the selection of Nicolas, a proselyte of Antioch, in Acts 6:5?
options: The gospel ministry includes Gentile converts as full participants in leadership
Only native-born Jews can hold church offices
Leadership was restricted to the twelve apostles alone
Gentiles were excluded from church community
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel ministry includes Gentile converts as full participants in leadership
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 names Nicolas, a proselyte (Gentile convert), among the seven leaders, showing early church openness to Gentile inclusion in ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is manifested in Acts 6:7 by the obedience of many priests to the faith?
questions.explanation: Acts 6:7 reports a great company of priests obeying the faith, demonstrating God's grace enabling even religious leaders to submit to Christ.

questions.question: What theological significance does the description of Stephen's face as 'the face of an angel' in Acts 6:15 carry?
options: It signifies divine approval and presence amid persecution
It indicates Stephen was literally an angel in disguise
It means the council was hallucinating
It shows Stephen was fearful and weak
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies divine approval and presence amid persecution
questions.explanation: Acts 6:15 depicts Stephen's countenance as angelic, signifying God's presence and approval as he faced false accusation and impending martyrdom.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the role of prayer and the Spirit in leadership appointment is taught by Acts 6:3 and Acts 6:6?
options: Church leadership is established through Spirit-filled character and prayerful commissioning
Leaders are appointed solely by popular vote without prayer
Prayer is unnecessary if leaders are wise
Human decision alone suffices for legitimate appointment
questions.correctAnswer: Church leadership is established through Spirit-filled character and prayerful commissioning
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3 calls for men full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom; Acts 6:6 shows apostles praying and laying hands on them, indicating Spirit and prayer are essential in leadership appointment.
